    //==
    // # Gradients and surface normals
    //
    // Bodies for the differentiable SDF interfaces
    // (`implicit-sdf.concepts.plato`). The gradient of an exact distance field is
    // its outward normal direction, so reporting one makes every gradient-derived
    // helper in `fields-implicits.library.plato` — `SurfaceNormalAt`,
    // `BoundaryNormalAt`, `SlopeAt`, `IsStationaryAt` — resolve against an SDF.
    //
    // None of the stored forms can be differentiated symbolically: `FunctionSdf*`
    // holds an opaque lambda and `SampledSdf*` holds a lattice, so both difference
    // the field numerically. `PlacedSdf*` is the exception — a rigid placement
    // rotates the source gradient rather than re-differencing it, which is the
    // whole reason the gradient travels through the interface instead of being
    // recomputed by each caller.

    // The finite-difference step used to estimate an SDF gradient. Far above
    // `Number.Epsilon`, where a difference quotient would be rounding noise rather
    // than signal, and well below the feature size the distance primitives are
    // written for.
    SdfGradientStep(_: Number): Number
        => 0.0001;

    // The gradient of a planar SDF by central differences: one forward and one
    // backward evaluation per axis, which cancels the first-order error term.
    // Precondition: step is positive.
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Finite_difference)
    NumericGradientAt(self: ISignedDistanceField2D, point: Point2D, step: Number): Vector2D
        => Vector2D(
            self.Eval(Point2D(point.X + step, point.Y)) - self.Eval(Point2D(point.X - step, point.Y)),
            self.Eval(Point2D(point.X, point.Y + step)) - self.Eval(Point2D(point.X, point.Y - step)))
           / (2.0 * step);

    // The gradient of a spatial SDF by central differences.
    // Precondition: step is positive.
    NumericGradientAt(self: ISignedDistanceField3D, point: Point3D, step: Number): Vector3D
        => Vector3D(
            self.Eval(Point3D(point.X + step, point.Y, point.Z)) - self.Eval(Point3D(point.X - step, point.Y, point.Z)),
            self.Eval(Point3D(point.X, point.Y + step, point.Z)) - self.Eval(Point3D(point.X, point.Y - step, point.Z)),
            self.Eval(Point3D(point.X, point.Y, point.Z + step)) - self.Eval(Point3D(point.X, point.Y, point.Z - step)))
           / (2.0 * step);

    // The gradient of a stored planar distance function, differenced numerically:
    // a lambda cannot be differentiated symbolically.
    GradientAt(self: FunctionSdf2D, point: Point2D): Vector2D
        => self.NumericGradientAt(point, Number.SdfGradientStep);

    // The gradient of a stored spatial distance function, differenced numerically.
    GradientAt(self: FunctionSdf3D, point: Point3D): Vector3D
        => self.NumericGradientAt(point, Number.SdfGradientStep);

    // The inner field's gradient. Bounds are ignored, exactly as Eval ignores them.
    GradientAt(self: BoundedSdf2D, point: Point2D): Vector2D
        => self.Sdf.GradientAt(point);

    // The inner field's gradient. Bounds are ignored.
    GradientAt(self: BoundedSdf3D, point: Point3D): Vector3D
        => self.Sdf.GradientAt(point);

    // The gradient of a sampled planar lattice, differenced numerically. Constant
    // within a cell up to the interpolation, so it is discontinuous at cell
    // boundaries — a bilinear field has no continuous gradient.
    GradientAt(self: SampledSdf2D, point: Point2D): Vector2D
        => self.NumericGradientAt(point, Number.SdfGradientStep);

    // The gradient of a sampled spatial lattice, differenced numerically. Same
    // per-cell discontinuity as the planar form.
    GradientAt(self: SampledSdf3D, point: Point3D): Vector3D
        => self.NumericGradientAt(point, Number.SdfGradientStep);

    // The gradient of a placed planar field: the source gradient turned by the
    // pose. Uniform scale cancels — it multiplies the distance and divides the
    // position by the same factor — so no scale term appears here.
    GradientAt(self: PlacedSdf2D, point: Point2D): Vector2D
        => self.Source.GradientAt(self.SourcePoint(point)).Transform(self.Pose);

    // The gradient of a placed spatial field: the source gradient turned by the
    // pose. Uniform scale cancels.
    GradientAt(self: PlacedSdf3D, point: Point3D): Vector3D
        => self.Source.GradientAt(self.SourcePoint(point)).Transform(self.Pose);

    // How far the field departs from being an exact distance at this point. An
    // exact signed distance field satisfies the eikonal equation, so its gradient
    // has unit length; a field that is only a lower bound, or not a bound at all,
    // does not. Zero means exact here. The residual is unsigned, so it reports the
    // departure without saying which side: a gradient shorter than unit makes a
    // raymarcher take shorter steps than the geometry requires, a longer one is
    // the field over-estimating distance and about to tunnel.
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eikonal_equation)
    EikonalResidualAt(self: IDifferentiableScalarField2D, point: Point2D): Number
        => (self.GradientAt(point).Magnitude - 1.0).Abs;

    // How far a spatial field departs from being an exact distance at this point.
    EikonalResidualAt(self: IDifferentiableScalarField3D, point: Point3D): Number
        => (self.GradientAt(point).Magnitude - 1.0).Abs;

    //==
    // # Ray marching
    //
    // Sphere tracing (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ray_marching): advance along
    // the ray by the current distance to the surface, which is the largest step
    // guaranteed to skip no geometry, and stop when that distance falls within
    // tolerance. Convergence therefore depends on the field being EXACT or a
    // LOWER BOUND (`implicit-sdf.concepts.plato`): a field that is NOT A BOUND
    // over-estimates, and a step taken on that value lands past the surface and
    // tunnels through it. `EikonalResidualAt` above measures the departure from
    // exact where the label is not trusted; a field that is k-Lipschitz for a
    // known k is safe to march once divided by k.
    //
    // A step budget bounds the work: a ray running nearly parallel to a surface
    // converges arbitrarily slowly, so exhausting the budget is a miss rather than
    // an error.

    // The ray parameter where sphere tracing converges, or `MissDistance` when the
    // budget runs out or the march passes `reach`. Recurses one step per advance.
    // Precondition: the ray direction is unit length; tolerance and reach are
    // positive; the field is exact or a lower bound — one that is not a bound
    // tunnels.
    MarchFrom(self: ISignedDistanceField3D, ray: Ray3D, t: Number, budget: Integer, tolerance: Number, reach: Number): Number {
        var distance = self.Eval(ray.PointAt(t));
        var next = t + distance;
        return distance.Abs <= tolerance
            ? t
            : (budget <= 0 || next > reach
                ? MissDistance()
                : self.MarchFrom(ray, next, budget - 1, tolerance, reach));
    }

    // Sphere-trace a ray against a spatial SDF. The hit normal is the field's own
    // unit gradient, so a field with an analytic gradient contributes it here
    // rather than being differenced again. Face, Barycentric and Uv are the
    // not-a-mesh values (`spatial-structures.types.plato`): an implicit surface has
    // no triangle to name. On a miss the normal faces back down the ray, matching
    // the broad-phase raycast convention. The reported normal is the true surface
    // normal only where the field is exact.
    // Precondition: the ray direction is unit length; tolerance and reach are
    // positive; the field is exact or a lower bound — one that is not a bound
    // tunnels.
    RayMarch(self: IDifferentiableSignedDistanceField3D, ray: Ray3D, budget: Integer, tolerance: Number, reach: Number): RayHit3D {
        var t = self.MarchFrom(ray, 0.0, budget, tolerance, reach);
        var hit = t < MissDistance();
        var position = hit ? ray.PointAt(t) : ray.Origin;
        return (hit,
                hit ? t : 0.0,
                position,
                hit
                    ? Direction3D(self.SurfaceNormalAt(position))
                    : Direction3D(-ray.Direction.Vector),
                FaceIndex(-1),
                BarycentricCoordinate(0.0, 0.0, 0.0),
                UvCoordinate(0.0, 0.0));
    }

    // The point on the surface nearest the query, by one Newton step along the
    // gradient: the point moved against its own normal by its own signed distance.
    // Lands on the surface in one step for an exact field; iterate for a lower
    // bound, and expect it to overshoot for a field that is not a bound.
    ProjectToSurface(self: IDifferentiableSignedDistanceField2D, point: Point2D): Point2D
        => point - self.GradientAt(point).Normalize * self.Eval(point);
